query: For high-entropy alloys intended for demanding engineering applications, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs the retention or loss of toughness, and why? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, the predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys, the room-temperature fracture toughness is governed by the stacking fault energy (SFE) which determines whether deformation proceeds by dislocation slip (high SFE), mechanical twinning (intermediate SFE), or martensitic transformation (low SFE). Alloys tuned to intermediate SFE exhibit enhanced work hardening via twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) and thus retain the greatest toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi single-phase FCC HEA, recrystallized, average grain size ~20 µm, baseline SFE ~20 mJ/m²
generation.intervention: Systematically vary Mn content from 10 at.% to 25 at.% to shift SFE from ~15 mJ/m² to ~35 mJ/m²
generation.conditions: Room-temperature uniaxial tensile and fracture toughness (K_IC) testing at 10⁻³ s⁻¹ strain rate; identical thermomechanical history
generation.structural_mediator: Stacking fault energy controlling the nucleation of deformation twins
generation.mechanism: At intermediate SFE (~25–30 mJ/m²), twins form during deformation, raising work-hardening rate and delaying crack initiation, whereas at low SFE (<15 mJ/m²) martensitic transformation embrittles and at high SFE (>35 mJ/m²) restricted slip reduces ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: K_IC will peak for alloys with SFE ≈25–30 mJ/m² (Mn ≈18 at.%), exceeding baseline K_IC (~120 MPa·m^0.5) by ~15–20%; alloys outside this SFE window will show 10–30% lower toughness.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi with SFE ≈20 mJ/m² and K_IC ≈120 MPa·m^0.5
generation.boundary: Valid for single-phase FCC HEAs with grain sizes 10–30 µm and SFE between 15–40 mJ/m²; breaks down if second phases form or grain size falls <5 µm or >50 µm.
generation.uncertainty: ±10% on SFE thresholds; toughness change magnitude ±15%

falsification_experiment.design: Produce HEA variants with SFE intentionally <15 mJ/m² (e.g., Mn >25 at.%) and >40 mJ/m² (e.g., add 5 at.% Al), process to the same grain size, then measure TWIP activity and K_IC under the same test conditions.
measurements: Stacking fault energy (via transmission electron microscopy and synchrotron XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If alloys with SFE <15 mJ/m² or >40 mJ/m² show equal or higher K_IC and similar twinning activity compared to intermediate-SFE alloys, the hypothesis is falsified.
